title: s28 transition rows complete;  s29 pin:  far-count structure at g in [2e8G, 1e11G],  best lognormal ~1e9G width ~1 decade;  turn-on (t-side) at (1e6, 1.5e6)G;  5e6G row reproduces exactly across runs
body: s28 delivered all six transition-window rows (5e5G, 7e5G, 1.5e6G, 3e6G, 5e6G, 7e6G; ~150-500 s each on the cached ledger stream). The s28 5e6G row -475565520 matches the s25 5e6G row exactly, cross-run reproducibility locked. The new 7e6G row: M = -484297184. Drift D(t) = M - (A ln t + B) against the clean 28-row ln law (1G..1e6G, max res 7719): +4214 @3e5G, +3307 @5e5G, +1363 @7e5G, -3148 @1e6G, -14840 @1.5e6G, -79947 @3e6G, -235575 @5e6G, -469687 @7e6G, -967966 @1e7G, -3.9e6 @2e7G, -2.44e7 @5e7G. Against the established 28-row ln law (1G..1e6G,  max  res  7719)  the  drift  is  small  POSITIVE  at  3e5G-7e5G  (the  (t/g0)^2  kernel-tail  signature  of  the  far  excess),  crosses  zero  at  t/G  in  (7e5,  1e6),  and  grows  NEGATIVE  t^2-like  beyond  (per-doubling  ratio  ~4.0  by  1e7G-2e7G);  the  sign  flip  is  the  t-side  fingerprint  of  a  far-side  count  excess  at  g0  >>  t  --  it  locates  where  the  kernel  tail  becomes  resolvable,  not  g0  itself.  (Against  s29's  re-fitted  near-face  anchor,  which  tilts  A/B  on  the  (G,  2.2G]  face  including  the  turning-on  rows,  the  apparent  crossing  moves  to  (5e6G,  1e7G);  anchor  artifact,  not  a  second  feature.) s29 (s27 machinery + s28 rows, 33 rows total): Part A min-norm still non-localizing (the census rows shift the far profile by a near-constant global mass offset only; no delta-e support above 3e-3) -- the ln-direction degeneracy, as in s27. Part B parametric family on the 12 far rows: P1 one-cell pole best 241345 at 2e8G, flat plateau [2e8G, 5e12G] at 2.4-2.9e5; P3 lognormal best 241143 at h0 = 1e9G sigma = 1.0 (plateau >= 1e9G); P2 power tail and P4 density fraction poor. Consolidated: positive far-side count structure at g in [2e8G, 1e11G] ~ (6e18, 3e21), best single configuration a lognormal centered ~1e9G (3e19) width ~1 decade, amplitude O(1e8..1e11) zeros; the s28 rows do NOT move the g-side window (P1 plateau 2e8G..5e12G,  P3 best 1e9G..1e11G --  the  s27  window)  because  every  measured  row  is  still  in  the  t  <<  g0  regime  where  g0  and  amplitude  compensate  over  ~3-4  decades;  what  s28  broke  is  the  t-side  turn-on  and  the  positive kernel-tail  bump  at  3e5G-1e6G,  which  is  the  first  data  BELOW  the  2e3G  census  onset. Important scope caveat on record: the certified zero ledger covers g up to ~1e9 (3.14e9 zeros), so the entire structure window is FAR ABOVE the ledger -- the drift is a statement about the RVM far-model region (smooth density model), i.e. either a genuine zero-density deviation there (the standing interpretation; standard density correction terms are far too small) or an unmodeled O(count-scale) far-model term (not excluded at current precision). The 5e7G row (t = 1.5e18) is at the engine's extreme-quadrature boundary -- rows beyond it need the extended-quadrature regime. Frontier statement:  breaking  the  g-side  position-amplitude  degeneracy  would  require  census  rows  at  t  comparable  to  g0  (t  ~  1e10G  ~  3e20),  ~200x  PAST  the  engine's  verified  1.5e18  extreme-quadrature  boundary  --  the  far-data  track  is  at  its  leveraged  wall  at  the  current  row  set;  the  window  [2e8G,  1e11G]  with  lognormal  sigma  ~1  best  fit  at  ~1e9G  stands  as  the  deconvolution's  answer  until  the  engine  boundary  moves.  The  t-side  turn-on  (7e5-1e6G)  remains  the  cleanest  s28  contribution,  and  the  exact  cross-run  5e6G  match  locks  the  census  channel. No RH claim.
